mock.title: CHAPTER 1 · A SQUARE AND A CUBE
question: 56 × k is a perfect cube. What is the
smallest
possible value of k?

tryit.text: Using pipes of 1 inch and 10 inches (up to 9 of each), how many pipes will it take to measure the height of a person who is 66 inches tall?
tryit.think: Picture measuring yourself with a ruler: count the tens first, then the ones.

tryit.text: X, Y and Z are single-digit whole numbers, and XY is a two-digit number. If 4000 < (XY)<sup>Z</sup> < 5000, what is the minimum possible value of XY?
tryit.think: Begin with Z: try Z = 2, then Z = 3. Which powers can land between 4000 and 5000?

tryit.text: How many possible combinations of 1 owl and 1 tree can be made from 3 owls and 5 trees?
tryit.think: Take one owl at a time. How many trees can it be paired with? Then add up for all three owls.

tryit.text: Sam has two different two-digit numbers. Both are divisible by 9, and neither is a multiple of 18. What is the LEAST possible sum of the two numbers?
tryit.think: Say it simply: “two-digit multiples of 9 that are not multiples of 18.” List the smallest ones.

tryit.text: What will come in place of “?” in the series 6, 26, 126, 626, ?
tryit.think: I know the powers of 5: 5, 25, 125, 625. Compare them with the series.

tryit.text: Why can’t we use the digit “2” when we write a number in binary?
tryit.think: Ask what a 2 would mean: two pipes of the same length. Could one pipe of the next length do the same job?

tryit.text: In 2020, Simran’s age was a multiple of 6. In 2024, her age was a multiple of 11. Which could be her age in 2024: 11, 22, 33 or 44 years?
tryit.think: Write it in numbers: if she is n in 2024, then n − 4 must be a multiple of 6.

backcover_intro: In Class 8, children take Computational Thinking further: spotting patterns in squares and cubes, turning a few examples into a general rule and working through logic puzzles step by step. These are not just computer skills. They are thinking skills for every subject.
